endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Primary victory alone does not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: Terminal outcome where candidate_m is elected mayor in the 2025 general election.
endpoint_ledger.label: Candidate M wins general election

meta.important_question: Will candidate_m win the 2025 general election for mayor?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the direct forecast-resolving endpoint implied by the corpus.
realization_criteria: official certified result or equivalent authoritative call shows candidate_m wins the general election for mayor
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Candidate M has partisan baseline support and primary victory but faces credible uncertainty from challenger recognition and issue attacks.

blockers: candidate_m coalition consolidates in late campaign
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is mutually exclusive with candidate_m_wins_general.
endpoint_ledger.description: Terminal outcome where someone other than candidate_m wins the general election for mayor.
endpoint_ledger.label: Candidate M loses general election

meta.important_question: Will candidate_m retain enough of the city_democratic_electorate to preserve the partisan baseline advantage by election day?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Binary terminal alternative required by the election resolution framing.
realization_criteria: official certified result or equivalent authoritative call shows former_governor_i or republican_nominee_r wins the general election for mayor
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Opponent name recognition and issue vulnerabilities create a credible loss path despite structural partisan disadvantage for challengers.

blockers: ideology or competence attacks trigger meaningful defections
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This can be realized even if margin is narrower than primary coalition expectations.
endpoint_ledger.description: Intermediate-but-outcome-relevant endpoint where candidate_m retains enough party-aligned support to keep baseline electoral advantage into election day.
endpoint_ledger.label: Democratic base consolidation holds

meta.important_question: Will former_governor_i become the clear principal alternative to candidate_m rather than merely a spoiler or secondary contender?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Coalition durability is a key causal gate to the final election result.
realization_criteria: pre-election indicators and final results show candidate_m wins a clear majority or dominant plurality among city_democratic_electorate proxies sufficient to preserve overall competitiveness
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Party registration advantage exists, but general-election transition introduces consolidation risk.

blockers: former_governor_i fails to convert recognition into trust or turnout
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Becoming principal challenger does not by itself imply winning the election.
endpoint_ledger.description: Outcome-relevant endpoint where former_governor_i clearly occupies the main anti-M lane and meaningfully contests victory.
endpoint_ledger.label: Former governor becomes principal challenger

meta.important_question: Will affordability-aligned and rent-burdened cohorts turn out at rates sufficient to offset attacks on ideology and experience?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint captures whether recognition translates into actual competitive structure.
realization_criteria: credible public evidence before election day shows former_governor_i consistently outpaces republican_nominee_r and attracts broad cross-pressured support as the main alternative to candidate_m
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Recognition is already nontrivial, but coalition breadth is not yet established.

Sparse packet gives high-level dynamics but not polling, endorsements, scandals, or institutional mechanics.
Terminal election outcome is clear, but many decisive process variables remain unobserved at T0.
Turnout uncertainty is central yet lacks quantitative baseline in corpus.

simulation_brief.decision_authority: citywide electorate determines outcome via general election
simulation_brief.primary_tension: structural partisan advantage for Candidate M versus cross-pressures from name recognition, ideological attacks, public-safety concerns, and turnout variability
simulation_brief.summary: A fictionalized citywide mayoral general election follows a major-party primary win by Candidate M, who ran on affordability. Candidate M faces a former governor running outside the major-party line and a Republican nominee. The electorate structurally leans toward Candidate M's party, but uncertainty remains around ideology framing, experience concerns, public-safety messaging, and turnout.
simulation_brief.terminal_condition: who wins the general election for mayor
